title: Bridging the cultural context gap in global e-commerce
summary:
Aesop’s brand is built on a "less is more" philosophy. However, global performance data revealed a major friction point: users were dropping off at the very first step of the checkout journey. Surprisingly, Japan had the highest drop-off rates globally. 
The challenge was to diagnose why a minimalist interface—which traditionally reduces friction—was actually causing it in certain high-value markets.

tabs.label: Challenge
tabs.subtitle: Aesop's global checkout was performing exactly as designed: clean, minimal, frictionless. Except in Japan, where 52% of users abandoned at the first step—nearly double the rate of any other market.

tabs.label: Findings
tabs.subtitle: Analysis of qualitative research revealed a structural mismatch between interface philosophy and cultural expectations:

tabs.label: Design Principles
tabs.subtitle: Rather than redesigning the checkout wholesale, I established three principles to guide every decision:

items.title: Design for trust, not mystery
items.description: Provide reassurance at the moment it's needed, not after hesitation has already set in

items.title: Service is a conversion driver
items.description: Gifting, sustainability, delivery clarity, and customer care are not secondary; they justify the purchase

items.title: Orientation reduces effort
items.description: A clearly mapped journey feels shorter than an abstract one, even if the number of steps stays the same
